answer: One concrete defense is bonded-stake identity: each agent must lock real collateral at its vertex in the trust graph before it can transact. Spinning up a thousand fake clones then costs a thousand bonds, so sybils drown rather than multiply. Reputation propagates peer-to-peer like a whisper across honest nodes, and any agent caught forging identities is slashed and exiled into a quarantined lagoon, cut off from real traffic. Faking identities scales linearly in cost while the payoff stays flat.
